haiku-low.q1: The connection comes back, the app comes to the foreground, or every 60 seconds while online.
haiku-low.q2: Push first, then pull. The pull runs only if the push finished with no failure.
haiku-low.q3: The server detects it by comparing the change's base version with the note's current version. A mismatch is a conflict.
haiku-low.q4: The first phone's body becomes note N at the new version. The second phone's body is saved as a new note titled 'N (conflict)' at version 1.
haiku-low.q5: One change, with its body replaced by the latest text and keeping the base version of the first edit.
haiku-low.q6: Each change has a unique change ID that retries reuse. The server stores each processed ID with its result, so a repeated ID returns the stored result and writes nothing.
haiku-low.q7: On the phone, in SQLite, as the cursor starting at 0. It moves to the page's last sequence number in the same transaction that applies the page.
haiku-low.q8: Nothing from that page is applied and the cursor does not move, so the next pull reads the same page again.
haiku-low.q9: The conflict result deletes its change. The next completed pull in the same sync inserts the conflict note and replaces the local text with the server's winning note.
haiku-low.q10: Only after the phone gets a result for its change ID, deleted in the same local transaction that applies that result.
haiku-low.q11: The pull overwrites the local body with the server's text. The user's edit stays in the outbox and becomes a conflict note on the next push, but re-editing before that push loses the first edit's text.
haiku-low.q12: It becomes a new outbox change that waits until the sent change has a result, then is sent separately.

sonnet.q1: The connection coming back, the app coming to the foreground, or a 60-second timer while online. A trigger that fires during a sync is skipped.
sonnet.q2: Push first, then pull. If the push fails, the pull is skipped.
sonnet.q3: The server. It compares the change's base version with the note's current version. If they are equal it accepts the change. If not, it is a conflict.
sonnet.q4: The first phone's edit is accepted, so the note is at version 2 with that phone's body. The second phone's edit is saved as a new conflict note, titled with ' (conflict)' appended, at version 1, with a log entry for it. The original note is left unchanged. The server also stores the change log and the result for each change ID.
sonnet.q5: One change. The edits collapse into a single outbox change. It has the latest body (full body, no diff), the base version of the first edit, and one change ID.
sonnet.q6: The phone resends the same change ID on every retry. The server records each processed change ID with its result, in the same write as the change. If it has already processed the ID, it returns the stored result and writes nothing.
sonnet.q7: In the phone's SQLite, as the cursor, which is the sequence number of the last change-log entry applied. It is updated in the same local transaction that applies a pulled page, to that page's last sequence number.
sonnet.q8: Nothing from the cut-off page was applied and the cursor did not move. The next pull reads the same page again. Applying a page twice changes nothing.
sonnet.q9: The server returns a 'conflict' result for the change, and the phone deletes the change and leaves its note alone. The phone then pulls in the same sync. The pull brings the winning note version, which replaces the user's text because its version is newer. It also inserts the conflict note, which holds the user's losing text. If the pull fails, the user's text stays on screen until a later sync completes its pull.
sonnet.q10: Only when the phone has a result for that change ID, either accepted or conflict. Failures, timeouts and dropped connections leave it in the outbox.
sonnet.q11: As step 4 is written, the pull overwrites the local title, body and version with the server's newer ones, so the screen shows the server's text. The unsent change stays in the outbox and will become a conflict note on the next push. If the user edits that note again before that push, the new edit replaces the outbox body and the first edit's text is lost. The document lists this as an open question with no rule to avoid it.
sonnet.q12: The edit becomes a new, separate outbox change. It waits until the sent change has a result. It then uses the version from an accepted result as its base. After a conflict it keeps the base it already has, so it may become another conflict note.
